title: Welsh–Powell bound on the chromatic number
statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on $n$ vertices, and enumerate its vertices as $v_1, v_2, \dots, v_n$ so that their degrees are arranged in non-increasing order, $d(v_1) \ge d(v_2) \ge \dots \ge d(v_n)$. Then the chromatic number of $G$ satisfies
\[
\chi(G) \;\le\; \max_{1 \le i \le n} \min\bigl\{\, d(v_i) + 1,\; i \,\bigr\}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: finite simple graph on n vertices
vertices enumerated by a bijection with Fin n
the enumeration lists degrees in non-increasing order
